## Summary

- Update `@vscode/codicons` from `0.0.46-44` to the published `0.0.46-46` prerelease in the root and web packages and lockfiles.
- Register the trophy glyph (`0xecf9`) added in microsoft/vscode-codicons#539.
- Replace the stacked/layers icon on the model picker's Compare Models toggle with the trophy. Keep the accessible label, tooltip, pressed-state behavior, and availability unchanged.
- Give the enabled comparison toggle a distinct theme-aware fill and border, separate from hover. Reserve the border inside the existing control size so toggling does not shift layout.
- Extend existing tests to verify the trophy, accessible pressed state, selected colors, and unchanged control dimensions when entering and leaving comparison setup.
- Show a single trophy in the configured comparison's composer control instead of one provider icon per attempt. Retain model and variant names in the hover and accessible label across expanded, compact, and minimal layouts; restore the normal model label when comparison is reset.
- Remove the unused per-attempt icon presentation contract and CSS.

Winner displays and metric badges are unchanged. The existing `copy-codicons` build task supplies the updated font; no custom font binary or release-infrastructure change is needed.

- `git diff --check` and `git diff --cached --check` — passed before commit.
- A Node assertion probe verified root/web manifest and lockfile consistency, all generated icon registrations against the published package, the copied font's byte identity, and the compiled trophy codepoint. Existing alias ordering was preserved rather than introducing unrelated generated-file reorderings.
- Visually checked the existing `SingleModelPicker` component fixture in dark, light, dark high-contrast, and light high-contrast themes. Activated the trophy toggle and verified comparison setup opens with the existing Compare Models accessible name and pressed state.
- Launched the current build in an isolated, authenticated Agents window and visually inspected the selected trophy toggle. Verified its active fill and border persist without hover, `aria-pressed` is true, and the control remains 28 × 28.
- Reloaded that Agents window with the composer fix and configured six distinct-model attempts. Visually verified exactly one trophy beside "Run 6 Attempts", all six model names retained in the accessible label, and clicking the trophy reopens comparison setup.

Integration/smoke tests and a live screen-reader session were not run locally. The four-theme fixture checks cover the trophy substitution; the final selected-state styling and six-attempt composer were visually checked in the live Agents window with the cloned profile's theme.

## Manual Test

With model comparison enabled in the Agents window, open the new-session model picker. Confirm the trophy appears beside Search; activate it to enter comparison setup. Move the pointer away and confirm the selected fill and border remain visible. Activate it again to return to single-model selection; the selected treatment should disappear without changing the control's dimensions.

Configure multiple comparison attempts and finish setup. Confirm the composer displays exactly one trophy instead of multiple provider icons or a joined model-name label. Hover the trophy to inspect the configured models and click it to edit the comparison. The send action should still report the configured attempt count. Repeat with variants of the same model and a narrow composer.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the model picker and enter or leave Compare Models setup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A single toggle click updates the in-memory comparison observable and synchronously calls TabbedModelPicker._showCurrent to rebuild the current picker before the changed setup view is usable. The diff changes only the tab action glyph and selected-state CSS; the existing list/DOM reconstruction remains on the same critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The existing rebuild scales with the in-memory provider/model list. The changed trophy glyph and two CSS rules remain constant-cost regardless of model count; comparison attempts are bounded at 10.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous UI event and one picker rebuild at a time; no queue, burst, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is introduced by the changed action.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Models and comparison state are already resident in memory. The diff neither adds a cache nor changes cold/warm picker behavior or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the click handler, synchronous _showCurrent call, changed icon assignment, and scoped CSS selector are directly visible in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact picker rebuild duration depends on installed model/provider count, but the diff does not increase that work or its frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed code substitutes one font glyph and styles one existing control without adding work inside the model-scaling rebuild.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the composer control after a comparison is committed, reset, or updated
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The comparison summary observable synchronously triggers ModelPickerWidget._renderLabel before the composer control reflects the new state. DOM replacement and existing geometry handling are on this UI path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Before the diff, a committed comparison mapped up to 10 attempt IDs, searched the model collection for each, created up to 10 icon nodes, and could measure the rendered label. After the diff, it creates one trophy node and suppresses the comparison text label while preserving the summary only in hover/accessibility metadata.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable updates are handled synchronously and serially in one autorun; no asynchronous fan-out or external boundary is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Cold and repeated summary updates use the same in-memory model and observable state; the diff removes the summaryModelIds dependency rather than adding retries or retained entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the removed per-attempt map/find/render path and the replacement constant icon path are explicit in the diff, and attempts are bounded by SESSION_COMPARISON_MAX_ATTEMPTS.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The removed work was bounded and likely small, but its exact DOM/layout cost is immaterial because the changed direction is reducing, not increasing, work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This path reduces repeated lookup, allocation, DOM-node creation, and label measurement work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load and display codicons in desktop or web builds
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shared codicon stylesheet loads codicon.ttf once before codicon glyphs can paint. The package upgrade changes the compile-time source of that existing font and registers one additional codepoint; it does not add another font resource or request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the packaged codicon.ttf resource referenced by the shared @font-face rule
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared font load on a cold resource load and no additional load per rendered trophy; warm cache behavior is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stylesheet loaded one codicon.ttf from the previous @vscode/codicons version.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing font load can gate codicon painting because font-display is block, but the PR does not add or duplicate this boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Font-load cardinality is constant and independent of the number of icons or comparison attempts. The diff adds one glyph registration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One existing font resource load per cold application resource load; no per-icon request. Warm browser/resource caches avoid repeating the transfer according to the existing resource cache.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resource URL and one-font architecture remain unchanged; cold loads still fetch/read one font and warm loads can use the existing resource cache. No cache key, negative-cache, or coalescing behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged resource cardinality and loading path; low evidence for any material byte-cost increase, so no finding is warranted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact byte delta of the prerelease font is not present in the supplied patch, but there is no evidence of a material size increase or extra request; one added glyph alone is insufficient to establish a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The dependency update replaces the contents of an already loaded single font rather than introducing a new startup/network boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and traced the changed composer render, comparison-toggle rebuild, and codicon resource-load scenarios. The UI changes are constant-cost or remove bounded repeated DOM/icon work; no actionable diff-introduced performance regression was found.
